meta.title: Agent runs that built this site
meta.source: OpenCode session store (local), exported by scripts/telemetry/export_traces.py
notes: One trace per user turn in the six root sessions of the website work; subagent runs nest under the task call that started them. Sessions are numbered S1, S2, … in the order they were created.
Times are milliseconds from the start of each trace. Only the calendar day is kept.
An LLM span is one model step, from its start to the start of its last tool call (an estimate of generation time). TOOL spans are the tool executions.

Published fields are structural only: span kind, generic agent name, model id, allowlisted tool name, times, status and token counts. Prompts, responses, reasoning, tool inputs and outputs, error messages, file names, commands and titles are not included.

Bash calls carry only a category (test, build, git-commit, git-other, server, other) assigned inside the exporter. Failed tool calls carry only an error class (timeout, not_found, permission, test_failure, bad_arguments, network, other) assigned inside the exporter from the error text, which is not kept.
Tools outside the allowlist were dropped entirely (25 spans). Unfinished calls (1) were dropped too.
Cost is omitted: the runs used a flat-rate subscription, so a list-price cost would mislead.

Evaluators are deterministic code checks. There is no LLM-as-judge: the exporter has no model access. Every pass/fail evaluation has a numeric score; its label follows from the evaluator's threshold and direction (meta.thresholds).

Long runs are compacted for size. Kept as single spans: the first and last 1 steps of each orchestrator run and 0 of each subagent run, every step that delegates or commits, and no step with an error in each run beyond those. The steps between are merged into CHAIN spans that keep their step, tool-call, error and token totals. Rollups, trace totals and evaluations use every span before compaction.
Round labels come from commit times in this repository's git history.

meta.dataset is a hash of every trace's id, day, session, duration and tool-call count. Human labels (data/human-labels.json, or a reviewer's download) carry it, and labels made on another dataset are set aside, because trace ids can shift between exports.

The OpenInference file has one line per published span; its timestamps put each trace's start at midnight UTC on the trace's real calendar day, so only the offsets are real. A merged (CHAIN) row with failed calls carries error.count and error.class.<class> counts and status ERROR, so the file's failed calls add up to the trace totals.

evaluators.name: Tool error rate
evaluators.description: Share of tool calls in the trace that returned an error. Fails above 10%. Score: the share (0–1).
evaluators.question: Did the agents mostly call their tools correctly?

evaluators.name: Recovered after error
evaluators.description: For every failed tool call, a later call of the same tool in the same trace succeeded. Score: the share of failed calls recovered (0–1). Only scored on traces with an error.
evaluators.question: When a tool call failed, did the agent retry or fix it?

evaluators.name: Delegation on large tasks
evaluators.description: On a large trace (at least 40 tool calls, or at least 3 edit/write calls, counted over the whole trace), subagents made at least half of the trace's tool calls. Score: the share of tool calls made by subagents (0–1). Small traces are not scored.
evaluators.question: On big jobs, did specialists do most of the hands-on work?

evaluators.name: Review before commit
evaluators.description: A quality-reviewer run finished after the previous commit in the session and before the trace's last commit. Score: 1 or 0. Only scored on traces that commit.
evaluators.question: Was the change reviewed before it was saved?

evaluators.name: Tests before commit
evaluators.description: A test command ran after the previous commit in the session and before the trace's last commit. Commands are classified inside the exporter; only the category is published. Score: 1 or 0. Only scored on traces that commit.
evaluators.question: Were the tests run before the change was saved?

evaluators.name: Checked after the last edit
evaluators.description: After the trace's last successful edit or write (by any agent, subagents included), a test, check or build command finished with exit code 0, or with no exit code recorded, before the trace ended. Score: 1 or 0. Only scored on traces that edit.
evaluators.question: Was the final state of the change tested or built?

evaluators.name: No stuck loop
evaluators.description: No agent run called the same tool and failed 3 or more times in a row (its calls in time order). Score: the longest such streak. Scored on traces with tool calls.
evaluators.question: Did an agent keep repeating a failing call?

evaluators.name: Changes after review
evaluators.description: Where a quality-reviewer run finished before a commit (the same interval as Review before commit), at least one edit or write followed a review and came before the next commit. A clean review with nothing to fix also fails, so read it as “the review changed something”. Score: the most edits that followed one review. Only scored when a review preceded the commit.
evaluators.question: Did the review lead to changes before the commit?

evaluators.name: Model latency budget
evaluators.description: p90 of model step latency (step start to its last tool call) in the trace is under 30 s. Score: the p90 in seconds.
evaluators.question: Did the model respond quickly enough to keep the loop moving?

evaluators.name: Generated tokens per tool call
evaluators.description: Output plus reasoning tokens divided by tool calls in the trace (a number, not pass/fail). Lower means terser actions.
evaluators.question: How much did the model write for each action it took?

evaluators.name: Parallel subagents
evaluators.description: The most subagent runs open at the same moment in the trace (a number, not pass/fail). Only scored on traces with a subagent run.
evaluators.question: How much work ran in parallel?

evaluators.name: Prompt cache reuse
evaluators.description: Cache-read tokens divided by all prompt tokens (input, cache read and cache write) over the trace's model steps (a number from 0 to 1, not pass/fail).
evaluators.question: How much of each prompt came from the cache?

evaluators.name: Most common error
evaluators.description: Each failed tool call is sorted into one class (timeout, not found, permission, test failure, bad arguments, network, other) by rules applied to its error text inside the exporter; the text is not published. Label: the most common class; score: its count. Only scored on traces with a failed call.
evaluators.question: What kind of failure was most common?
